math_steps.note: Entry refraction bends light toward normal; internal path meets exit face at angle θ_i2
math_steps.code:
// 2. Dual-interface refraction: entry angle and internal prism apex constraint
val sinThetaR1 = sin(thetaI1Rad) / nLambda
val thetaR1Rad = asin(sinThetaR1.coerceIn(-1f, 1f))
val thetaI2Rad = apexAngleRad - thetaR1Rad
math_steps.sub_desc: Applies Snell's law at first boundary and enforces internal prism apex constraint.

math_steps.formula: δ(λ) = θ_i1 + θ_r2 - α  (TIR if sin(θ_i2) ≥ 1 / n)
math_steps.note: Second refraction amplifies angular spread; steep rays undergo Total Internal Reflection
math_steps.code:
// 3. Exit angle, total chromatic deviation and critical angle TIR check
val sinThetaR2 = nLambda * sin(thetaI2Rad)
val isTIR = sinThetaR2 >= 1f
val thetaR2Rad = if (!isTIR) asin(sinThetaR2.coerceIn(-1f, 1f)) else 0f
val deviationAngleRad = thetaI1Rad + thetaR2Rad - apexAngleRad
math_steps.sub_desc: Calculates exit refraction, total angular deviation, and internal reflection threshold.

mystery.en: Why does a clear triangular glass prism split pure white light into seven vibrant rainbow colors?

en.title: Prism Dispersion & Newton's Rainbow
en.teaser: Passing white light through a triangular glass prism separates each wavelength into a stunning rainbow spectrum.

en.hook: Why does shining plain white light through clear glass create a full rainbow spectrum?
en.math: Inside glass, high-frequency violet light travels slower than red light, giving it a higher refractive index and bending it more sharply at both prism faces.
